findings.description: When a slot is an out-of-office delegation, the API includes fromUser.id as a number (IFromUser.id), but the new slot response declares it as string. A consumer of useAvailableSlots following this type and calling a string method on fromUser.id will throw; use number to mirror the server type.
findings.failureMode: Out-of-office slot consumers are promised string user IDs but receive numeric IDs and may crash.
findings.title: Use numeric out-of-office user IDs in slot response

findings.description: The list endpoint selects Availability.days as Int[] but the new local response declares string[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes schedules to getScheduleListItemData, whose argument requires days: number[], so the atoms package fails type checking when compiling the schedule list; declare days as number[].
findings.failureMode: TypeScript build of the mainline schedule list fails assigning string[] to number[].
findings.title: Match Prisma's numeric availability days

findings.description: The new noRestrictedImports glob now forbids @calcom/trpc/components/*, but two unchanged atoms wrappers still import QueryCell from @calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell. Running Biome lint on atoms therefore fails on both wrappers; migrate those imports to a non-TRPC module or adjust the restriction with an intentional exception.
findings.failureMode: Linting atoms reports noRestrictedImports errors for two existing wrappers.
findings.title: Update the existing atoms TRPC component imports before restricting them

findings.description: The new './booker/types' export points to './booker/types.ts', but the package's files allowlist publishes only dist, globals.min.css and fonts. npm pack excludes booker/types.ts, so an installed consumer importing the new subpath fails module resolution; publish this file or point the export to its declaration under dist.
findings.failureMode: Installed @calcom/atoms cannot resolve the newly advertised @calcom/atoms/booker/types entry point.
findings.title: Point the new booker type export at a published file

findings.description: The new validator uses single-quoted strings (lines 40 and 46), while the repository Biome JavaScript formatter mandates double quotes. Formatting checks on this new TypeScript file fail; switch these literals to double quotes.
findings.failureMode: Biome format --check on the changed TypeScript file exits nonzero.
findings.title: Format the new validator to match the Biome configuration

findings.failureMode: Biome format biome.json fails on both changed TRPC import groups.
findings.title: Format the new restricted-import groups in biome.json

findings.description: Declaring the unexported SlotInfo after existing exported types triggers Biome's useExportsLast warning in booker/types.ts. The repo's pre-commit lint treats warnings as errors, so commits/checks on this changed file fail; place SlotInfo above the exports or use a declaration order Biome accepts.

findings.title: Move the new private slot type before exported declarations

findings.description: `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()` no longer starts with XCTest's `test` prefix; the FullFunctionalTestPlan includes this suite without skipping the method, but XCTest will no longer discover or execute its iOS 17 bookmark-to-Reminders assertion. Rename the method back to `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders()` while addressing flakiness in the interaction, not by removing the test.
findings.failureMode: A FullFunctionalTestPlan run reports no result for bookmark sharing to Reminders on iOS 17 even if that feature regresses.
findings.title: Keep the bookmark Reminders test discoverable

findings.description: On iOS 17+, the new `return` makes every iPad onboarding test and the iPhone bottom-placement test finish without either `app.terminate()` or `super.tearDown()`. Even an iPad test skipped at its first statement has already launched Firefox in `setUp()`, so the supposedly completed/skipped case leaves the app running and skips superclass cleanup. Only guard the theme reset; always fall through to teardown.
findings.failureMode: Run `testSelectBottomPlacement` on an iOS 17 iPad: setUp launches Firefox, the test throws XCTSkipIf, then tearDown returns; Firefox is still running after the skipped test.
findings.title: Do not return before app and XCTest teardown

findings.description: The bookmark view's `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` uses the 0.5-second default minimum, and presents the context menu only in `.began`. The new 0.5-second press releases exactly when the gesture becomes eligible, so on a run where the timer fires after release none of the identical retries can show the menu; bookmark share tests fail waiting for it. Use a duration above the recognizer threshold, as the previous 1.0-second press did.
findings.failureMode: When a 0.5-second press ends before the default 0.5-second gesture timer reaches `.began`, the context menu never appears and bookmark share tests fail.
findings.title: Press past the bookmark gesture threshold

findings.description: The patch is now 10.0.1 but `Baseline.Designer.props` remains at 9.0.0; this line turns off `EnsureBaselineIsUpdated` instead of bringing it to the previous release. The 9.0.0 baseline includes `System.Text.Json` for `Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup` while that project's current references have no such entry; when this now-servicing build runs, BUILD002 reports the missing baseline reference and fails. Regenerate the baseline from 10.0.0 and keep validation on (it also prevents skipped patch packages resolving as 9.0.0).
findings.failureMode: 10.0.1 AzureAppServices.HostingStartup build fails BUILD002 on stale 9.0.0 System.Text.Json baseline reference
findings.title: Refresh the 10.0.0 baseline before switching to servicing

The macOS-15 image has Xcode 16.x and no 15.2, so `xcode-select` fails before the build. Point the public job at its installed Xcode 16.4 path.

findings.failureMode: official macOS-15 pipeline fails at xcode-select before building
findings.title: Fix Xcode selection on official macOS-15 jobs

findings.failureMode: servicing builds beyond patch 1 pass despite removed baseline dependency
findings.title: Keep BUILD002 protection for every servicing patch

findings.description: Changing the declaration from `namespace ...;` to `namespace ... {` violates the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule and emits IDE0161, configured as a warning in this repo. For a normal `eng/build.sh`/`msbuild.sh` build of the E2E project (both default to warnings-as-errors), the build fails; preserve the file-scoped declaration while quarantining the test.
findings.failureMode: E2E project build with repository build scripts fails on IDE0161 warning-as-error
findings.title: Retain a file-scoped namespace in WebSocket E2E tests

findings.description: Changing `testBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` to `verifyBookmarksShareNormalWebsiteReminders` silently removes the iOS 17 bookmark-to-Reminders check from XCTest's automatically discovered tests (including FullFunctional), so that share flow can regress while the suite reports success. Keep a `test`-prefixed method instead of renaming it out of test discovery.
findings.failureMode: The FullFunctional UI suite silently loses the bookmark-to-Reminders test on every run.
findings.title: Keep the bookmark Reminders check discoverable by XCTest

findings.description: On iOS 17+ iPad, `testFirstRunTourDarkMode` calls `switchThemeToDarkOrLight("Dark")`, but this new `|| iPad()` branch skips the former Light reset. `DefaultThemeManager` saves the manual theme in `UserDefaults.standard`, which the UI-test profile reset does not clear; subsequent iPad tests launch in Dark rather than Light. Do not exempt the dark-mode tour from restoring Light.
findings.failureMode: Running the iPad dark-mode onboarding tour then another UI test preserves the wrong persistent theme.
findings.title: Reset the iPad theme after the dark-mode tour

findings.description: On iOS 17+ this return is taken by every iPad onboarding test and iPhone bottom-placement test, bypassing `app.terminate()` and `super.tearDown()` below. The test runner leaves Firefox running instead of cleaning up, potentially contaminating the next UI test; skip only the theme reset and still execute the cleanup.
findings.failureMode: On iPad or the bottom-placement iPhone case, teardown leaves the application running and omits inherited cleanup.
findings.title: Keep teardown cleanup when skipping theme reset

findings.description: The bookmarks panel's `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` has the UIKit default 0.5s minimum and only shows the menu on `.began`. This changes the test press from 1s to exactly 0.5s, so on a busy simulator where the touch-up is processed before recognition, *every* retry is too short and the bookmark sharing tests fail waiting for Context Menu. Retain a duration safely above 0.5s while retrying.
findings.failureMode: Bookmark sharing tests intermittently time out waiting for Context Menu when release wins the 0.5-second gesture recognition race.
findings.title: Use a long press longer than the 0.5s recognizer minimum

findings.description: If an injected executor returns `{"result": None}` (or omits `result`), this adapter returns None despite declaring `str`; the next `len(rendered)` raises an uncaught TypeError instead of producing a failed NodeRunResult. The submitted code also fails `make type-check` with `str | None` not assignable to `str`. Reject None with the other non-string values before returning.
findings.failureMode: Uncaught TypeError in template node and failing registered basedpyright check
findings.title: Treat null template results as a render error

findings.description: For a template-transform subclass registered as version `2` and a node config with `version: "2"`, the factory resolves that subclass in `matched_node_class` but this hard-coded branch still creates v1 TemplateTransformNode. A small reproduction that registers a v2 subclass returned `created v2? False TemplateTransformNode`, so the workflow executes the wrong version. Instantiate the resolved class (only passing `template_renderer` when supported) instead of unconditionally constructing v1.
findings.failureMode: Factory ignores a registered template-transform version and instantiates v1
findings.title: Preserve version dispatch when injecting a renderer

findings.description: An injected renderer implementing render_template but having __len__ == 0 or __bool__ == False is a valid Jinja2TemplateRenderer; both the factory at line 63 and TemplateTransformNode at line 41 use `or`, so they replace it with CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer. A workflow configured with this renderer invokes the sandbox instead and returns the wrong output or fails. Use an explicit None check at both sites.
findings.failureMode: Valid false-y renderer is ignored and default code executor called instead
findings.title: Do not discard a false-y injected template renderer

findings.description: The newly added constant-first mixed-list assertion triggers SIM300; running the registered Ruff check without fixes fails at this line. Put `result.outputs['output']` on the left.
findings.failureMode: make check fails with SIM300 Yoda condition
findings.title: Fix the reversed new assertion flagged by Ruff

findings.description: The added `test_run_with_string_concatenation` signature is not in Ruff's canonical format; `make lint` reformats this exact changed signature, so `ruff format --check` would fail on the submitted file. Use the single-line signature required by Ruff.
findings.failureMode: ruff format --check fails for added test signature
findings.title: Format the new concatenation test signature

findings.description: The added `test_run_with_conditional_if_else` signature is not in Ruff's canonical format; `make lint` reformats this distinct changed signature, so `ruff format --check` fails on the submitted file. Use the single-line signature.
findings.failureMode: ruff format --check fails for added test signature
findings.title: Format the new conditional test signature

findings.description: The new adapter returns `None` when an injected `code_executor` returns `{}` or `{"result": None}`; its `isinstance` guard explicitly skips None. `TemplateTransformNode._run` then calls `len(None)` and crashes instead of producing a failed node result. The focused basedpyright run also reports `str | None` cannot satisfy its `str` return annotation. Reject `None` alongside other non-strings.
findings.failureMode: Injected code executor returning absent/null result leads to unhandled TypeError during template node execution; type-check fails.
findings.title: Reject null template results before returning

findings.description: `make check` runs `ruff check`, which reports SIM300 on the new reversed assertion at line 1031 and exits nonzero. Put `result.outputs["output"]` on the left so the registered check passes.
findings.failureMode: make check fails on SIM300 for the added assertion.
findings.title: Fix the new assertion rejected by Ruff

findings.description: When `template_renderer` implements `__len__` and is empty (or otherwise has false boolean value), this `or` replaces it with the sandbox adapter; the same fallback occurs for direct TemplateTransformNode injection at template_transform_node.py:41. A caller supplying e.g. an empty caching renderer sees the wrong renderer used and an unexpected sandbox invocation. Test `is not None` in both places.
findings.failureMode: Explicitly injected falsy renderer is silently ignored, producing wrong output or reaching external code execution.
findings.title: Preserve explicitly supplied falsy renderers

findings.description: `ruff format --check` fails on this added function because its one-line signature fits the configured width; the formatter rewrites lines 662–664. Collapse the signature to the formatter's one-line form so formatting checks pass.
findings.failureMode: ruff format --check rejects the new concatenation test signature.
findings.title: Use Ruff-formatted signature for concatenation test

findings.description: `ruff format --check` also fails on this newly added test signature and rewrites it to one line. Format this site so the formatting check accepts the file.
findings.failureMode: ruff format --check rejects the added conditional test signature.
findings.title: Use Ruff-formatted signature for conditional test

findings.description: Connections select ClickZetta's `cz.sql.string.literal.escape.mode = 'quote'`, while this f-string produces SQL `ESCAPE '\\'` containing **two** literal backslashes. SQL ESCAPE takes one character, so when full-text MATCH_ALL fails and `_search_by_like` is invoked, even a plain keyword query errors instead of returning fallback results. Emit one backslash in quote mode or parameterize the escape character.
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta full-text fallback fails at query execution with invalid two-character ESCAPE expression
findings.title: Use a one-character ClickZetta ESCAPE literal

findings.description: `WorkflowRun.inputs`/`outputs` are written with `json.dumps` (default `ensure_ascii=True`), so a run with input `中文` stores `\u4e2d\u6587`. The removed `unicode_escape`/`\\u` conversion matched that JSON text, but `escape_like_pattern` now passes raw `中文` to `.ilike`, returning no log for a previously searchable input. JSON-encode the keyword for those two JSON text columns before escaping LIKE metacharacters (keep the raw form for session IDs).
findings.failureMode: workflow log keyword search returns zero results for non-ASCII content in JSON inputs or outputs
findings.title: Keep JSON-encoded Unicode matching in workflow log search

findings.description: With `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX=false`, the fallback runs `escape_like_pattern('50%')`, producing `50\%`, but declares `ESCAPE '|'`. Thus the literal backslash is required and `%` is still a wildcard; querying a stored `50% discount` document yields no match (or wrong hits for other texts). Generate a `|`-escaped pattern or use backslash as the SQL escape character.
findings.failureMode: IRIS no-index fallback returns missing or incorrect hits for literal special-character queries
findings.title: Match IRIS ESCAPE character to generated pattern

findings.description: On MySQL with `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES`, a `not contains` filter for `a%` calls `escape_like_pattern` to produce `a\%`, but this `notlike` omits `escape='\\'`. MySQL then has no default escape and looks for a literal backslash before a wildcard, so a document with metadata `a%` is incorrectly included. Add `escape='\\'` here as in the other metadata LIKE cases.
findings.failureMode: metadata exclusion fails to filter values containing literal percent/underscore in MySQL NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES mode
findings.title: Pass an explicit escape in the negated metadata LIKE

findings.description: The `.readerMode` tap dispatches `showReaderMode`, but this changed reducer line maps it to `.readerModeLongPressAction`. BVC then calls `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which writes the page to the reading list instead of `toggleReaderMode()` to enter or leave Reader Mode. Restore `.readerMode` for `handleShowReaderModeAction`; keep the long-press mapping only in `handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction`.
findings.failureMode: Regular reader-mode toolbar taps and accessibility magic taps unexpectedly save the page to the reading list and never toggle Reader Mode
findings.title: Reader-mode tap adds a reading-list entry instead of toggling

findings.description: The default toolbar state has `readerModeState == nil`, so this new `default: true` is sent to `ToolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped`. Its existing extras constructor writes `isEnabled` into `isPrivate`: a normal-tab reader button tap now records `isPrivate: true`, and the unchanged `testDidTapButton_tapOnReaderModeButton_dispatchesShowReaderModes` fails its `XCTAssertEqual(savedExtras.isPrivate, false)`. Revert the flipped switch results; the pre-existing swapped extras mapping is a separate issue, not a justification for the flip.
findings.failureMode: Existing reader-mode toolbar middleware test fails and analytics claims non-private clicks are private
findings.title: Reader-mode telemetry inversion breaks the tap test and mislabels normal tabs

findings.description: On a tab with `http://localhost/reader-mode/page?url=...`, tapping Cancel, tabs, or menu passes the tab's internal reader URL in `ToolbarAction.cancelEdit`. `AddressBarState` prefers that non-nil value over the original `tab.url?.displayURL` already in state, and the location field formats its host as `localhost` (and shows the internal URL when edited). Keep the display URL/leave the action URL nil for reader-mode tabs instead.
findings.failureMode: Toolbar shows localhost rather than the visited site's origin after canceling edit mode on a reader page
findings.title: Canceling editing on Reader Mode displays localhost as the site

findings.description: `Path::extension()` is never both `json` and `json5`, so `&&` skips schema validation for every normal config. For example, `{"identifier":"com.example.app","productName":"/tmp/Important"}` deserializes (the regex exists only in the schema), whereas the old CLI rejected the slash; a macOS build passes that name to `bundle_project`, where `Path::join` targets `/tmp/Important.app` and `remove_dir_all` deletes it if present. Restore the `||` guard.
findings.failureMode: Schema-invalid productName becomes absolute macOS bundle path; existing unrelated /tmp/Important.app directory deleted on build.
findings.title: Restore JSON/JSON5 validation to prevent unsafe bundle paths

findings.description: A valid `tauri.conf.json` stores `identifier` at the top level and `bundle` is an object, so `get("bundle").as_str()` always yields None. `mobile::write_options` then fails with `app configuration is missing an identifier` on normal Android/iOS dev/build runs (and the Xcode/Android option reader cannot locate the server address). Keep `get("identifier")`.
findings.failureMode: Normal Android/iOS dev/build fails to write/read CLI options because original_identifier is None.
findings.title: Keep reading the top-level identifier for mobile options

findings.description: The new 156-column `let schema = ...expect(...)` expression is left unwrapped despite `rustfmt.toml` setting max_width=100; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` will require changing this line and fail the formatting gate. Format the initializer with rustfmt.
findings.failureMode: Required rustfmt check fails on unformatted new initializer.
findings.title: Format the new validator initializer for rustfmt

findings.description: `ValidateBaseline=false` lets the new servicing build use the still-9.0.0 `Baseline.Designer.props` even though `PreviousAspNetCoreReleaseVersion` is now 10.0.0. For example, that baseline lists `System.Text.Json` for `Microsoft.AspNetCore.AzureAppServices.HostingStartup` whereas its 10.0 project no longer references it: `ResolveCustomReferences` treats this as an unused servicing dependency and raises BUILD002 on an unchanged project. Regenerate the baseline from 10.0.0 and keep validation enabled.
findings.failureMode: The 10.0.1 servicing build fails BUILD002 for a 9.x dependency removed in 10.0.0, or packages against an outdated baseline.
findings.title: Update the 10.0 release baseline rather than disabling its check

findings.description: Changing the hosted macOS image to macOS-15 (and internal image on line 322) leaves both build steps selecting `/Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer` even though macOS-15 has only Xcode 16.x and newer (the changed step labels say 16.4). Both macOS builds fail at `xcode-select` before running the build; update both selection commands to the Xcode 16.4 directory alongside the image change.
findings.failureMode: Both macOS-15 builds fail with xcode-select invalid developer directory.
findings.title: Fix Xcode selection when changing both macOS build images

findings.description: Changing this file to a block-scoped namespace breaks the required file-scoped namespace rule and triggers IDE0161 (configured as warning in `.editorconfig`). When the Components E2E project is built with `EXECUTE_COMPONENTS_E2E_TESTS=true` under CI's warnings-as-errors mode, the E2E build fails; preserve the original file-scoped declaration.
findings.failureMode: Components E2E CI build fails with IDE0161 treated as error.
findings.title: Keep the E2E test namespace file-scoped

findings.description: For a 10.0.2 or later servicing build that drops a baseline package reference, the added `AspNetCorePatchVersion == '1'` condition prevents BUILD002 from firing, so a servicing package can ship with a broken dependency contract; keep the guard active on all servicing patch versions.
findings.failureMode: A later servicing update with a removed baseline reference builds and ships instead of failing BUILD002.
findings.title: Keep servicing reference-removal guard for later patches

findings.description: Wrapping the already-main-actor `handleAction` in `Task` defers `.forward*Card` completion. `OnboardingViewCompact.handleBottomButtonAction` posts `.screenChanged` immediately after the action returns, so VoiceOver announces/focuses the old card instead of the next one when Next is tapped; it used to advance synchronously first. The same deferral allows Skip to finish the flow before a queued final-card action runs, causing duplicate completion. Call `handleAction` directly on the main actor rather than queueing it.
findings.failureMode: On compact onboarding with VoiceOver, tap the forward button: `.screenChanged` fires before `pageCount` advances, announcing the old card. If Skip is invoked before the task runs, deferred completion can finish the flow twice.
findings.title: Keep forward actions synchronous before announcing the next card

findings.description: SelectLightTheme sets the Light control, but this now reads darkThemeView while expecting "1"; with Light selected the Dark value is "0", so testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails before it can check Dark/Automatic. Read lightThemeView as before.
findings.failureMode: UI test fails for normal Light selection
findings.title: Assert Light instead of Dark after selecting Light

findings.description: Opening Shortcuts pushes `TopSitesSettingsViewController`, which has no Done navigation item; the Done button belongs to Homepage/main Settings. With `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` moved below `app.buttons["Done"].waitAndTap()`, the test tries to tap Done while still on Shortcuts and times out, never reaching its checks. Back out to a screen showing Done before tapping it, then reset the navigator to NewTabScreen.
findings.failureMode: testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection waits on missing Done button on Shortcuts screen
findings.title: Navigate to the homepage before dismissing settings

findings.description: Deleting `checkCopiedUrl()` leaves `testClipboard` with no clipboard-content assertion on iOS 15: that helper compared the copied URL on pre-iOS 16, while the remaining paste-and-compare branch runs only on iOS 17+. If Copy stops writing the URL, the test now reports success on iOS 15. Restore the call.
findings.failureMode: iOS 15 clipboard regression passes the UI test
findings.title: Preserve clipboard verification on iOS 15

findings.description: For compact onboarding, a forward button invokes `handleBottomButtonAction`, then immediately posts `UIAccessibility.screenChanged`. Before this change, `onActionTap` synchronously called `handleAction`, whose forward case updates `pageCount` before that post. Scheduling `handleAction` in an unawaited `Task` makes the notification run while the old page is still selected, so VoiceOver is directed to the stale card instead of the new one on each forward action. It also permits stale Settings/popup actions after Skip has completed. Call the main-actor action inline to preserve ordering.
findings.failureMode: VoiceOver screen-change event is posted while previous onboarding page is selected, causing focus on the wrong card; fast Skip can also allow an action to run after dismissal
findings.title: Do not defer onboarding page changes past the accessibility notification

findings.description: With tab-swipe enabled, the toolbar leading edge is now tied to the right skeleton's trailing edge while its trailing edge is tied to the same right skeleton's leading edge. Since the right skeleton has a positive width this forces a negative width for the central toolbar; Auto Layout breaks constraints or the main address bar disappears/mispositions. Restore the left skeleton trailing anchor.
findings.failureMode: Main address bar collapses or Auto Layout emits unsatisfiable constraints on tab-swipe-enabled screens.
findings.title: Pin the main toolbar to the left skeleton, not the right

findings.description: When trailing page action buttons are first added or moved into the trailing stack, `updateActionStack` sets their alpha to zero. The layout update repeats `browserActionStack` instead of visiting `trailingPageActionStack`, so those page actions remain invisible despite being present and tappable; enumerate the trailing stack here.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page action (e.g. reload or reader-mode control) stays invisible after toolbar configure; initial toolbar layout too.
findings.title: Restore trailing page buttons' alpha after configuration

findings.description: `locationDividerView` is constrained directly before `trailingPageActionStack`, but this changed check consults `leadingPageActionStack`. For a BrowserAddressToolbar configured with `.default()` UX (4pt divider) and only a trailing page action, the divider is wrongly 0pt; with only a leading action it adds 4pt of empty space before a nonexistent trailing action. Base the width on the trailing stack, as before.
findings.failureMode: Edge-case BrowserKit toolbar configurations with leading-only or trailing-only actions render the URL/action separator with the wrong width.
findings.title: Use trailing actions to determine URL divider width

findings.description: `lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js` is still the filename on disk. Loading members-api now attempts the nonexistent `lib/magic-link/magic-link` and raises MODULE_NOT_FOUND during startup. Restore this require to the actual `MagicLink` filename.
findings.failureMode: loading members API crashes with MODULE_NOT_FOUND for magic-link
findings.title: Require the actual MagicLink filename

findings.description: `EmailEventStorage.js` was not renamed in this change, so when email analytics initializes, `require('../email-service/email-event-storage')` throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the service fails to start. Keep the old module path until that file is actually renamed.
findings.failureMode: email analytics init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for email-event-storage
findings.title: Require the existing email event storage module

findings.description: `EmailEventProcessor.js` is not renamed by this PR; once the storage require is fixed, initializing email analytics still throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on `../email-service/email-event-processor`. Restore the actual filename in the require.
findings.failureMode: email analytics init throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND for email-event-processor
findings.title: Require the existing email event processor module

findings.description: Lines 1–4 and 6–10 drop their semicolons while changing module paths. `plugin:ghost/node` enforces `semi: ['error', 'always']`, so linting the server fails on these imports; restore their terminators.
findings.failureMode: ghost/core lint:server rejects nine unterminated const imports
findings.title: Preserve semicolons on renamed Members API imports

findings.description: Prisma defines `Availability.days` as `Int[]`, while this new response type declares `string[]`. `ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper` passes these schedules to `getScheduleListItemData`, which requires `days: number[]`; this yields a TypeScript type error on the normal schedule-list path. Use `number[]` to match the API model.
findings.failureMode: Type-check fails in ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper for string[] not assignable to number[] on each schedule availability.
findings.title: Use numeric availability days in the copied schedule response

findings.description: `useAvailableSlots` now types the response with `fromUser.id: string`, but the server/`IGetAvailableSlots` supplies numeric `IFromUser.id`. Passing `schedule.data` to `useAvailableTimeSlots` in the calendar view fails TypeScript assignability for the optional `fromUser` property (and clients assuming a string on an OOO slot will receive a number). Mirror the server type's `number`.
findings.failureMode: Type-check of EventTypeCalendarViewComponent fails: GetAvailableSlotsResponse not assignable to IGetAvailableSlots (`fromUser.id` string vs number).
findings.title: Keep the OOO fromUser id numeric in the slots response

findings.description: `./booker/types` now resolves to `./booker/types.ts`, but the package `files` whitelist only publishes `dist`, `globals.min.css`, and `fonts`. `npm pack --dry-run` confirms `booker/types.ts` is absent. Consumers installing the published atoms package and importing the new subpath get a module-not-found error; include the target in the npm package (or point the export at a file under dist).
findings.failureMode: Published @calcom/atoms package cannot resolve the newly advertised @calcom/atoms/booker/types export.
findings.title: Include the new booker/types export in the published package

findings.description: The new `@calcom/trpc/**` restriction matches `@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell`, which both atoms wrappers still import. Running Biome lint on those wrappers reports two `noRestrictedImports` errors, so full-package lint fails; migrate both imports before enabling the new restriction.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint of both atoms wrappers exits with two noRestrictedImports errors.
findings.title: Migrate remaining atoms imports before broadening the TRPC ban

findings.description: Adding non-exported `SlotInfo` after the already exported booker types triggers Biome `useExportsLast` warning. The pre-commit lint command uses `--error-on-warnings`, so staging this file now fails that check; place the private type before the exports or export it.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint with --error-on-warnings fails for booker/types.ts due to newly introduced useExportsLast warning.
findings.title: Move the new private SlotInfo declaration before exports

findings.description: The shorter new TRPC patterns remain on separate lines, but Biome formats each group as a one-line array. `biome format --config-path=biome-staged.json biome.json` exits nonzero, and lint-staged runs it for the changed JSON file; format this override (including the already unformatted `includes` array) before staging it.
findings.failureMode: Staging the changed biome.json makes the configured JSON formatting pre-commit check fail.
findings.title: Format the modified Biome import patterns

findings.description: The new validator uses single-quoted TS strings on lines 39–46 despite this repository's Biome double-quote configuration. `biome format packages/platform/atoms/hooks/schedules/types.ts` exits nonzero on this file, so format checks fail; format the literals using Biome.
findings.failureMode: Running Biome format check on the added file fails with one formatting error.
findings.title: Format new schedule validator with configured double quotes

findings.description: When `HINCRBYFLOAT` updates a field with an expiration, dropping `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` makes `hashTypeSet` persist it on the primary (`hfieldPersist` for hashtables, `HASH_LP_NO_TTL` for listpackex). E.g. `HSETEX k EX 100 FIELDS 1 f 1; HINCRBYFLOAT k f 1.1` makes `HTTL k FIELDS 1 f` return -1 on the primary even though the replica still has the original TTL; after 100s replica/failover loses a field that primary retains. Restore `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` on this local write.
findings.failureMode: Expiring field becomes persistent on primary but expires on replica; a failover after its TTL loses a field and primary retention violates the API.
findings.title: Keep the primary field's TTL during HINCRBYFLOAT

findings.description: The new definition of `addHashFieldToReply` removes `static`, although every caller remains in `t_hash.c` and there is no public declaration. This breaks the repository rule for file-local helpers and produces `-Wmissing-prototypes` (a build error with `-Werror -Wmissing-prototypes`). Retain `static`.
findings.failureMode: A build enabling missing-prototype warnings as errors now fails at t_hash.c:2576; the formerly private symbol is exported unnecessarily.
findings.title: Restore static linkage to the hash reply helper

findings.description: All five `write_and_make_executable(...)?` calls are in `prepare_tools() -> crate::Result<PathBuf>`, but the new helper returns `Result<_, FileWriteError>` and crate::Error has no From<FileWriteError> variant/impl. This prevents tauri-bundler compiling (E0277), before bundling can run; return io::Result like before or add an appropriate conversion/variant.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler compilation fails at ? operators due to absent From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error
findings.title: Convert FileWriteError into the bundler error

findings.description: On an empty tools cache, the first download of AppRun reaches set_permissions on a nonexistent destination and returns ENOENT before fs::write; every first AppImage bundle fails. Restore the original write-then-chmod order.
findings.failureMode: fresh cache fails AppImage bundling with Failed to set permissions: No such file or directory
findings.title: Write new tool files before setting permissions

findings.description: With tools already cached but no GTK script, this guard skips the included script altogether; linuxdeploy invoked with --plugin gtk cannot find it and fails, even once file writes are corrected. Use !gtk.exists() (or install script unconditionally).
findings.failureMode: missing gtk tool and cached other tools => linuxdeploy fails to locate gtk plugin
findings.title: Create GTK plugin when absent

findings.description: If pkg-config reports `/usr/lib64/gtk-3.0/...` or `/usr/lib64/gdk-pixbuf-2.0/...` (e.g. Fedora), `${file/\/usr\/lib\//}` does not strip that prefix; `ln -s` therefore writes absolute links in AppDir/usr/lib pointing back to host `/usr/lib64` instead of bundled modules. On another machine lacking the same host plugins, the GTK/Pixbuf modules are missing. Normalize `/usr/lib64` and multilib paths before linking, as the formerly downloaded plugin did.
findings.failureMode: Fedora-built AppImage GTK modules resolve to the build host instead of packaged copies
findings.title: Keep GTK module links inside the AppDir on lib64 hosts

findings.description: After replacing the downloaded GTK plugin, this script goes straight from GLib schemas to GTK modules and omits the former `echo "Installing GIRepository Typelibs"`, `copy_lib_tree "$gi_typelibsdir"`, and `GI_TYPELIB_PATH` hook. For a Tauri AppImage with a sidecar or extension using GIRepository (e.g. PyGObject), a target without host GTK typelibs fails to import them. Restore the packaging and hook steps.
findings.failureMode: AppImage GTK/GObject introspection consumers fail to load typelibs on machines without host installation
findings.title: Retain GIRepository typelibs in GTK bundles

findings.description: On GNOME configured with `color-scheme='prefer-dark'` but a GTK theme named `Adwaita`, `gtk-theme` contains no `dark`, so the new AppRun hook forces `GTK_THEME=Adwaita:light`. The plugin previously downloaded by the base bundler uses the desktop portal/GSettings color-scheme and would choose dark; preserve that check instead of guessing from gtk-theme.
findings.failureMode: AppImage starts with light GTK theme on systems with dark-mode preference
findings.title: Detect dark preference from the color scheme

findings.description: Even if the missing `From<FileWriteError>` conversion is fixed separately, this new error enum still manually implements `Display` and `Error`, violating the base AGENTS.md mandate that custom error enums derive `thiserror::Error` with #[error(...)] annotations. Derive thiserror instead; a compliance gate enforcing that repository contract would reject this error type as written.
findings.failureMode: error-handling compliance review rejects the manual enum instead of the mandatory thiserror derive
findings.title: Derive the new error type using thiserror

findings.description: Setting `strict: false` implicitly disables `strictNullChecks`, which TanStack Router's typings require. `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` now reports `"strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json"` across router tests (244 errors vs 2 with strict restored). Both `validate:types` and `build` run tsc, so they fail, and the change also bypasses mandated strict checking. Restore strict mode.
findings.failureMode: UI type validation and build fail with hundreds of TanStack Router errors under strict:false.
findings.title: Keep strict checking enabled so the UI can typecheck

findings.description: The new global `parseInt(e.target.value)` violates `useNumberNamespace: error` in ui-v2's Biome config; `biome check` reports an error here and the UI v2 CI `biome ci` lint job will fail. It also silently truncates decimal threshold input (e.g. `1.5` becomes `1`) unlike the other trigger fields. Use `Number(e.target.value)` consistently (or otherwise ensure valid integer input) to avoid both failures.
findings.failureMode: Required UI v2 Biome CI job fails on the new field; fractional input silently changes the submitted threshold.
findings.title: Make the work-pool threshold pass the Biome CI check

findings.description: In the Proactive ("Stays in") posture, selecting Ready saves it as `expect` with no `after`. On a Ready event the server counts it as a satisfied expected event rather than starting a stay-in-status window; if the pool then becomes Not Ready, that event is ignored and a later window can fire despite the pool no longer being Ready. Bind the selected status to `after` for Proactive, as the deployment and flow-run forms do.
findings.failureMode: Proactive pool status trigger can fire after the pool already left the chosen status.
findings.title: Use `after` to watch a work pool staying in a status

findings.description: In Proactive ("Stays in") mode the selected work-queue status is written to `expect`, leaving `after` empty. After the queue enters Ready, a subsequent Not Ready event does not match `expect` and does not cancel the no-Ready-event window; the automation can fire even though the queue left Ready. Store this selection in `after` when Proactive, as in deployment/flow-run status fields.
findings.failureMode: Proactive queue trigger can fire after the queue already left the chosen status.
findings.title: Use `after` to watch a work queue staying in a status

findings.description: Selecting Ready reactively then switching to `Stays in` leaves the old `expect: ['prefect.deployment.ready']` alongside the new `after: ['prefect.deployment.ready']`. A later Not Ready event is filtered out, and the automation can fire even though the deployment already left Ready. Switching back leaves a stale `after` as well, requiring a second Ready event for a supposedly reactive trigger. Clear the inactive field when posture changes.
findings.failureMode: Switching deployment posture retains stale after/expect and yields false or missed status automation firings.
findings.title: Clear the inactive deployment status filter on posture change

findings.description: `''.split('\n')` returns `[""]`, so `lines.length > 0` never takes the unset branch: clearing a typed custom event list leaves `expect: [""]`. The wizard schema accepts the value, but the server's `expects()` will not match normal event names, leaving the resulting reactive automation inert instead of restoring the empty (any-event) list. Drop blank entries and write `[]` when cleared.
findings.failureMode: Custom automation no longer triggers after user clears the expected-events textarea.
findings.title: Clear an empty custom event list instead of saving an empty event name

findings.description: The new deployment/work-pool/work-queue/custom proactive `Within` inputs all use `min={0}` and the wizard Zod schema accepts 1–9, yet the server EventTrigger validator rejects any nonzero proactive window below 10 seconds. For example, selecting a new deployment status trigger, switching to Proactive and entering 5 passes wizard validation but produces a trigger rejected on creation. Validate at least 10 seconds when Proactive (including in the form schema).
findings.failureMode: Proactive triggers with 1–9 seconds pass new wizard validation but fail server validation on creation.
findings.title: Reject sub-10-second proactive windows in new trigger forms

findings.description: `FormControl` passes the form-label id to the Radix Select root, not to its trigger. The new deployment status combobox has an empty accessible name (confirmed by `toHaveAccessibleName('Status')` failure) and the visible label cannot focus it; screen-reader users have no indication what this control changes. Give `SelectTrigger` a linked id/aria-label.
findings.failureMode: Deployment status select is exposed to screen readers as an unnamed combobox.
findings.title: Associate the deployment status dropdown with its label

findings.description: `FormLabel` says Status but this `<SelectTrigger>` never receives an id or accessible name; `FormControl` gives its id to the Select root instead. The visible label does not focus or identify the work-pool combobox, leaving screen readers with an unnamed select. Set its trigger id/aria-label.
findings.failureMode: Work-pool status select has no accessible field name.
findings.title: Associate the work-pool status dropdown with its label

findings.description: The new work-queue `<SelectTrigger>` has no id or accessible name, while `FormControl` attaches the form-label id to the Radix Select root. The status combobox is therefore unnamed for screen readers and the visible Status label cannot focus it. Set the accessible label/id directly on the trigger.
findings.failureMode: Work-queue status select has no accessible field name.
findings.title: Associate the work-queue status dropdown with its label

findings.description: With `SET foo bar` in cluster mode, `numkeys` is 1; `j == 1` reads the zero-initialized extra key position (argv[0], `SET`), writes past the one-int buffer, and returns CROSSSLOT instead of executing the command. With more than six keys, `keys[j]` itself is past the allocated array and can crash the server. Change `<=` back to `<`.
findings.failureMode: Normal one-key cluster writes rejected and out-of-bounds heap write/read can crash the server
findings.title: Keep the slot loop within the extracted key count

findings.description: Every keyed cluster command now calls direct malloc (line 1110) and direct free (lines 1120/1124) for an unused slot buffer, violating the mandated Redis allocator wrappers and bypassing maxmemory accounting. On a process allocation failure the unchecked NULL is written in the loop, terminating the server even if the off-by-one is fixed. Remove the buffer and both frees.
findings.failureMode: Server crash from NULL buffer on allocation failure independent of the loop boundary, plus bypassed memory tracking
findings.title: Remove unchecked and untracked per-command allocation

findings.description: The previous `if !gtk.exists()` downloaded the plugin only if missing. The inverted condition now skips inlining it on a fresh cache, so linuxdeploy's mandatory `--plugin gtk` cannot find it; on a reused cache containing a custom GTK plugin it replaces the script, and if that file is a symlink it overwrites the linked target too. Restore the missing-file guard so clean caches get the script and existing assets remain intact.
findings.failureMode: Clean-cache bundling fails, or reused cache destroys existing/custom GTK plugin (potentially symlink target)
findings.title: Do not overwrite an existing GTK plugin or skip a missing one

findings.description: `prepare_tools` returns `crate::Result<PathBuf>` and uses `?` on the helper, but this new return type is `FileWriteError` and `crate::Error` has no `From<FileWriteError>` conversion. Building tauri-bundler on Linux fails with E0277 at every call site; add a conversion to the bundler error type before propagating this error.
findings.failureMode: Linux tauri-bundler compilation fails with E0277 for FileWriteError
findings.title: Convert FileWriteError before using `?` in prepare_tools

findings.description: With an empty tools cache, `prepare_tools` passes a nonexistent AppRun path to this helper. `set_permissions` runs before `fs::write` creates it, returning NotFound and failing every fresh AppImage bundle. Restore the write-before-chmod order.
findings.failureMode: Fresh AppImage bundle fails at AppRun creation with No such file or directory
findings.title: Write newly downloaded tools before setting their permissions

findings.description: This new `set_permissions(...).map_err(...)` expression is 101 columns; rustfmt's formatter splits before `.map_err`, so the repository's required `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this changed line. Wrap it using cargo fmt.
findings.failureMode: Required cargo fmt --check rejects changed code
findings.title: Rustfmt-wrap the new chmod call

findings.description: The added `FileWriteError` is a custom error enum with hand-written `Display` and `Error` implementations, violating the repository's mandatory thiserror rule; an error-type compliance check fails on this new type even if its conversion into `crate::Error` is fixed separately. Derive `thiserror::Error` with `#[error(...)]` messages instead of manual impls (or reuse `std::io::Error`).
findings.failureMode: Mandatory custom error compliance check rejects manually implemented Error enum
findings.title: Derive thiserror for the new custom error enum

findings.description: The newly checked-in GTK script uses four-space indentation (e.g. this `verbose` assignment) although `.editorconfig` mandates two spaces for all files. A repository EditorConfig compliance check on the added file fails; format the script with two-space indentation.
findings.failureMode: EditorConfig validation rejects newly added GTK script
findings.title: Format new GTK script with EditorConfig indentation

findings.description: The newly checked-in GStreamer script uses four-space indentation throughout despite `.editorconfig` mandating two spaces for all files. An EditorConfig check on the newly added script fails; format it with two-space indentation.
findings.failureMode: EditorConfig validation rejects newly added GStreamer script
findings.title: Format new GStreamer script with EditorConfig indentation

findings.description: The extension cannot be both `json` and `json5`, so every JSON/JSON5 config skips validation. With `productName: "/tmp/valuable"` on macOS, serde accepts the string even though the bundled schema forbids `/`; `tauri bundle` passes it to the bundler, whose `.join("/tmp/valuable.app")` resolves outside the output directory and `remove_dir_all` deletes any existing `/tmp/valuable.app`. The previous `||` rejected the config before bundling. Restore the OR condition.
findings.failureMode: data loss when a schema-invalid product name redirects macOS bundle cleanup outside output directory
findings.title: Restore schema validation to prevent unsafe bundle paths

findings.description: For any normal `tauri.conf.json` with top-level `identifier` and object `bundle`, reading `bundle` as a string yields `None`. `mobile::write_options()` then fails with `app configuration is missing an identifier` on every Android/iOS dev/build; `mobile::read_options()` also panics via `.expect(...)` when the Gradle/Xcode script starts. Read `config.get("identifier")` again.
findings.failureMode: mobile commands fail or panic on valid configuration
findings.title: Restore the top-level identifier lookup before mobile builds

findings.description: If `merge_with` is called on a loaded handle with a new `--config` override (e.g. `{ "productName": "New" }`), it mutates only the temporary JSON `value`, records the extension, and returns `Ok(handle)` without updating `config_metadata.inner`, so reading the returned handle still yields the original product name. Restore `config_metadata.inner = serde_json::from_value(value).context("failed to parse config")?` before returning.
findings.failureMode: standalone post-load merge falsely succeeds and returns unchanged configuration
findings.title: Keep the live Config in sync in `merge_with`

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` exits 1 and shows rustfmt splitting the long `serde_json::from_str(...).expect(...)` statement. Format this helper to let the required Rust formatting gate pass.
findings.failureMode: Rust format gate fails
findings.title: Format the validator helper for the required Rust check

findings.description: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` also flags this new `.extensions.insert(...)` line and exits 1; format this statement (separately from the helper initializer) to pass the mandatory rustfmt check.
findings.failureMode: Rust format gate fails on merge_with insertion
findings.title: Format the extension insertion for the required Rust check

findings.description: `strict:false` disables `strictNullChecks`, which the TanStack Router types explicitly require. Type validation/build now emit `"strictNullChecks must be enabled in tsconfig.json"` across router consumers, and ESLint flags all four new `useWatch` assignments as unsafe `any`; the new lint errors disappear when `strict:true` is restored. Keep strict checking enabled.
findings.failureMode: Type validation and lint fail under the new TS configuration.
findings.title: Re-enable strict mode to unblock UI validation

findings.description: For 'Stays in Ready', the pool select writes Ready to `expect` rather than `after`. After a Ready event starts its per-pool bucket, a Not Ready event during the window is ignored because it does not match `expect`; the proactive bucket can then fire while the pool is Not Ready. Save the selected status in `after` for Proactive posture, as the deployment/flow-run fields do, so a subsequent pool status event cancels the stay-in window.
findings.failureMode: Pool Ready -> Not Ready before the window ends can still trigger 'Stays in Ready'.
findings.title: Track proactive pool transitions via after

findings.description: For 'Stays in Ready', the queue select writes Ready to `expect` instead of `after`. After a Ready event initializes the queue bucket, a subsequent Not Ready transition is ignored because it does not match `expect`; the proactive bucket can fire while the queue is Not Ready. Save the selected status to `after` for Proactive posture so a change of queue status cancels the stay-in window.
findings.failureMode: Queue Ready -> Not Ready before the window ends can still trigger 'Stays in Ready'.
findings.title: Track proactive queue transitions via after

findings.description: If a user selects Reactive/Ready, switches to Proactive, then selects Ready again, `expect` from the first selection persists alongside the new `after`. The backend ignores a Not Ready transition because it does not match `expect` and can fire 'Stays in Ready' even after the deployment became Not Ready. Clear the opposite field on posture change; likewise remove stale `after` on a return to Reactive.
findings.failureMode: Changing deployment trigger posture leaves an old field that causes an incorrect firing.
findings.title: Clear stale deployment criteria when switching posture

findings.description: Each status select initially has an empty value, while the template defaults omit `expect`/`after` and Zod makes both optional. A user who selects a deployment, pool or queue status template and presses Next without choosing an option gets a trigger with no status filter; Reactive then matches any event on that resource rather than one selected status. Require a selection or provide a valid initial status.
findings.failureMode: Leaving the status dropdown blank yields an overbroad trigger that passes validation.
findings.title: Require a status before continuing with a status template

findings.description: After a user clears a previously entered custom event, `"".split("\n")` still has one element, so `expect` becomes `[""]` rather than empty. The schema accepts this, but the backend matches no actual events against the empty string, so a reactive custom trigger silently stops firing. Filter empty lines and set an empty array when the textarea is cleared.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom event input silently produces a never-firing reactive trigger.
findings.title: Do not store an empty custom event name on clear

findings.description: All four newly added templates accept a Proactive `within` of 1–9 seconds (e.g. 5) via `min={0}` and their Number onChange; the wizard schema also permits these values, so Next accepts the trigger. The server `EventTrigger` validator rejects Proactive windows below 10 seconds, meaning the generated automation cannot be created. Constrain the new inputs and form validation to >=10 seconds for Proactive.
findings.failureMode: A proactive trigger with within=5 passes wizard validation but is rejected by the backend.
findings.title: Reject proactive within values below backend minimum

findings.description: For a valid number input containing `1e2`, `parseInt` stores threshold 1 instead of 100, so the work-pool automation fires after one event instead of 100. It also fails Biome's `useNumberNamespace` check. Use `Number(e.target.value)` as in the parallel components.
findings.failureMode: Valid exponent input silently saves a smaller threshold, firing a work-pool automation early.
findings.title: Avoid truncating work-pool threshold inputs

findings.description: All three new status selects wrap the Select root in `FormControl`, but the Radix button `SelectTrigger` has no id/aria-label. A `getByLabelText('Status')` query fails even though a visual Status label is present; assistive-technology users cannot identify these dropdowns. Attach the label to the actual trigger in deployment, pool and queue components.
findings.failureMode: Status dropdown lacks an associated accessible label.
findings.title: Connect status labels to select triggers

findings.description: The repository requires `component.test.tsx` next to every new React component. There is no `custom-trigger-fields.test.tsx`, so `vitest run .../custom-trigger-fields.test.tsx` finds no test and the textarea-to-array conversion cannot be checked independently (blank lines already escape the display-only TriggerStep tests). Add the corresponding co-located component test.
findings.failureMode: Direct component test invocation has no test file; custom event array behavior is untested.
findings.title: Add a co-located CustomTriggerFields test

findings.description: This new React component lacks the mandated `deployment-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx` alongside it, so running its component suite yields no tests and the reactive/proactive status mapping is not checked by the new TriggerStep display-only tests. Add the co-located test.
findings.failureMode: Direct component test invocation has no test file; the status array and posture behavior remain untested.
findings.title: Add a co-located DeploymentStatusTriggerFields test

findings.description: The newly added pool component has no mandated `work-pool-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx`; `vitest run` on that component's path finds no test, and neither value-to-array conversion nor the proactive event choice is exercised by the new display-only TriggerStep test. Add its co-located test.
findings.failureMode: Pool component tests cannot run at the mandated location; pool event behavior remains untested.
findings.title: Add a co-located WorkPoolStatusTriggerFields test

findings.description: The new queue component lacks its required `work-queue-status-trigger-fields.test.tsx` alongside it; a component-specific test run finds no tests, and the added TriggerStep display assertions cannot catch miswired proactive queue events. Add the co-located test.
findings.failureMode: Queue component test run has no tests; its event output is unverified.
findings.title: Add a co-located WorkQueueStatusTriggerFields test

findings.description: With tab swiping enabled, rightSkeletonAddressBar starts at container.trailingAnchor, so constraining toolbar.leadingAnchor to rightSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor puts it beyond the right edge while toolbar.trailingAnchor remains at rightSkeletonAddressBar.leadingAnchor. This gives an inverted/offscreen toolbar instead of one spanning the container. Retain the leftSkeletonAddressBar.trailingAnchor attachment.
findings.failureMode: Toolbar disappears/breaks its layout when tab-swiping feature is enabled.
findings.title: Anchor main toolbar to left skeleton, not right

findings.description: When updateActions installs a new trailing-page button, updateActionStack initializes it with alpha = 0. updateToolbarLayout now adds browserActionStack a second time instead of trailingPageActionStack, so that button never gets alpha = 1 and stays invisible whether animated is true or false. Include trailingPageActionStack in stacks.
findings.failureMode: New trailing page actions become invisible after configuration.
findings.title: Restore trailing page actions to layout fade list

findings.description: With a trailing page action and no leading page action, updateActionSpacing now zeroes dividerWidthConstraint although the divider lies between locationView and trailingPageActionStack. When a leading action exists but no trailing action it instead inserts an unnecessary gap. Check trailingPageActionStack, as before the rename.
findings.failureMode: Wrong divider spacing when leading and trailing page action presence differs.
findings.title: Base divider spacing on trailing page actions

findings.description: After SelectLightTheme, the assertion reads darkThemeView instead of lightThemeView. With mutually exclusive Light/Dark choices it sees 0 and the UI test fails even though the app switched correctly; use lightThemeView.
findings.failureMode: Selecting Light leaves Dark unselected, so testCheckSystemThemeChanges fails at the first assertion
findings.title: Read the Light theme selection from the Light control

findings.description: After opening Shortcuts, the test remains on `TopSitesSettingsViewController`. This child is pushed and has no Done button; only `HomePageSettingViewController` supplies one. Moving `navigator.goto(NewTabScreen)` after the Done tap means `waitAndTap()` times out before either the navigation or the assertion, so `testDisableTopSitesSettingsRemovesSection` fails. Back out of Shortcuts to the Homepage settings first, then tap Done.
findings.failureMode: Running the homepage shortcuts test on iPhone times out looking for Done on the child Shortcuts settings page
findings.title: Return from Shortcuts before tapping Done

findings.description: `GET foo` has one key, but `j <= numkeys` runs a second iteration; the initialized unused key position is 0 (the `GET` command), whose hash slot differs from `foo`, so a valid request returns CROSSSLOT. It also writes `slot_buffer[1]` past the one-element allocation (and larger results can read invalid argv), risking a server crash/corruption. Use `j < numkeys`.
findings.failureMode: Cluster GET foo returns CROSSSLOT instead of the value, plus one-past-end heap write; keys[1].pos=0 and slots differ (12182 vs 12405).
findings.title: Do not hash an extra key past the result

findings.description: The default build (also `make REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror"`) fails at this deprecated `malloc` call, and temporary allocations are missing from Redis memory accounting. Use zmalloc.
findings.failureMode: The default build fails in cluster.c at the changed malloc call; allocation bypasses tracking.
findings.title: Replace deprecated malloc with zmalloc

findings.description: Both early (line 1120) and normal (line 1124) exits call deprecated `free`, so the default build and the `-Werror` build fail on both. Change both to `zfree` paired with `zmalloc`.
findings.failureMode: The default build stops in cluster.c at free on lines 1120 and 1124.
findings.title: Replace both deprecated free calls with zfree

findings.description: `@calcom/features/ee/teams/services/teamService` is a TypeScript-only source module, not the compiled platform library export used by the parallel org invite controller. A built Nest API loads the bare package import with Node, which cannot resolve extensionless `teamService` to a JS file; Biome also rejects this API-v2 import as forbidden. Import `TeamService` from `@calcom/platform-libraries` to prevent the production API startup and lint failures.
findings.failureMode: Built platform API fails to load the new endpoint's module on startup (and new controller fails Biome's noRestrictedImports rule).
findings.title: Import TeamService through the supported compiled library

findings.description: `TEAM_MEMBER` on a link-issuing POST lets a regular team member request a link and invite arbitrary new users; it contradicts the team-admin-only contract and the added 403 test. Use `TEAM_ADMIN` so the guard rejects non-admins.
findings.failureMode: Authenticated MEMBER of a team successfully creates shareable invitation tokens for the team instead of receiving 403.
findings.title: Require team admin, not team member, for invite creation

findings.description: For an org subteam whose parent organization has Admin API disabled, `/v2/organizations/:orgId/teams/:teamId/invite` is forbidden by `IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard`, but this new route uses only `ApiAuthGuard` and `RolesGuard` and calls the same `TeamService.createInvite(teamId)`. A team admin can use `/v2/teams/:teamId/invite` to bypass that entitlement and create invites anyway. Check the org entitlement for org-context teams on this path too.
findings.failureMode: Authenticated admin of an org subteam without Admin API access generates working invite links via the generic team endpoint despite the org invite endpoint denying them.
findings.title: Apply the org Admin API entitlement when inviting org subteams

findings.description: A newly created invitation returns `newToken.identifier` (`invite-link-for-teamId-${teamId}`) in `data.token` even though the URL and stored verification token contain the randomly generated `token`. Callers sharing `data.token` cannot redeem it, and subsequent invocations for the same team return the same purported token. Return `newToken.token` or `token`.
findings.failureMode: On any new invite, the returned token is not valid for TeamService.inviteMemberByToken and does not match the invite URL.
findings.title: Return the generated verification token, not its identifier

findings.description: With `isOrgContext` false for a regular team, the changed `if` now emits `/signup?token=...` instead of `/teams?token=...`; signed-in recipients are redirected off signup to `/`, while unsigned recipients get the non-email identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-N` prefilled as an email. Org/subteam invites instead go to `/teams`, which redirects unauthenticated recipients to login rather than the org signup flow. Restore the previous `!isOrgContext` condition.
findings.failureMode: New invite links do not let regular-team members join via the teams page or prospective org members sign up directly.
findings.title: Do not invert the team/organization invite routes

findings.description: `@Post('/invite')` adds `/v2/teams/{teamId}/invite`, but the checked-in `docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json` still lists only the organization invite route; Mintlify reads that checked-in file. After release, the API exists but the published API v2 reference and generated clients built from it omit the route. Regenerate and commit the spec for the new endpoint.
findings.failureMode: Public API reference / spec-driven clients don't expose the new endpoint although the route is live.
findings.title: Publish the new invite route in the checked-in OpenAPI spec

findings.description: The Swagger property says every returned `inviteLink` opens signup and gives only a `/signup?...` example, but `TeamService.buildInviteLink` can return `/teams?token=...` based on team context. For an org/subteam with current code, Swagger tells API consumers the wrong route; with the service condition restored the regular-team case remains wrong. Document conditional team/org links rather than always signup.
findings.failureMode: Generated OpenAPI/Swagger for an invite link misrepresents the URL returned for one team context, so consumers following the documented route use the wrong join flow.
findings.title: Document both possible invite-link destinations

findings.description: On a Reader Mode toolbar tap, `.showReaderMode` reaches this reducer, which now sets `.readerModeLongPressAction` instead of the removed line `displayView: .readerMode`. BVC handles this by calling `toggleReaderModeLongPressAction()`, which writes the selected page into the reading list; it never calls `toggleReaderMode()` to open/close Reader Mode. Restore `.readerMode` here; keep `.readerModeLongPressAction` in the separate add-to-reading-list handler.
findings.failureMode: Tapping Reader Mode saves the page to Reading List instead of opening/closing Reader Mode.
findings.title: A Reader Mode tap now adds the page to Reading List

findings.description: The new default `true` is fed as `isEnabled` to `ToolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped`, which assigns `isEnabled` to Glean's `isPrivate` extra. In the standard test setup (normal tab with nil reader-mode state), the event now reports `isPrivate: true`, so the unchanged reader-mode telemetry test expecting false fails; likewise a private tab with `.available` now reports non-private. Restore the previous switch booleans in this hunk so this regression and failing test are fixed (the extra's parameter mix-up elsewhere is pre-existing).
findings.failureMode: Existing reader-mode toolbar telemetry XCTest fails on its default normal-tab state, and emitted private-mode flag is false for a private available tab and true for a normal active tab.
findings.title: Do not invert Reader Mode telemetry while extras use the old mapping

findings.description: For a Reader Mode tab, `tab.url` is `http://localhost:.../reader-mode/page?url=...`. After canceling address-bar editing (including menu/tab-tray taps), the new `||` forwards that raw URL in `ToolbarAction.cancelEdit`; `AddressBarState` takes it instead of its prior decoded display URL and `LocationView` renders `config.url?.absoluteString`. The user sees the localhost reader URL rather than the article address. Pass `currentURL.displayURL` when restoring the address bar in Reader Mode.
findings.failureMode: Cancel editing or open menu on a Reader Mode article changes the address-bar text from article URL to internal localhost URL.
findings.title: Decode the Reader Mode URL before restoring the address bar

findings.description: The new endpoint is guarded by `TEAM_MEMBER`, not `TEAM_ADMIN`; if the guard authorizes regular members at that level, a regular team member can create/share an invitation link to add outsiders without admin permission, and the new non-admin 403 E2E fails. Set the role to `TEAM_ADMIN`.
findings.failureMode: An authenticated MEMBER of a team sends POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite and receives a working invitation despite lacking team admin rights.
findings.title: Require TEAM_ADMIN to create invite links

findings.description: `TeamService.createInvite` accepts org subteams, but this new route has only team-role and auth guards. For a non-platform org missing an `organizationSettings` row, the existing `/v2/organizations/<orgId>/teams/<teamId>/invite` denies access in `IsAdminAPIEnabledGuard` while `/v2/teams/<teamId>/invite` issues a working token to the same org-subteam admin. Add an equivalent org-access check on the new route for org-context team IDs.
findings.failureMode: For an org subteam of an org missing organizationSettings, an admin obtains an invitation from /v2/teams/:teamId/invite while the existing organization route responds Forbidden.
findings.title: Enforce org API access on org-context invites

findings.description: A fresh invite is persisted with a random `token` but `createInvite` returns `newToken.identifier` (`invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`). The endpoint returns a token different from the one in the link; successive requests return the same token and clients using `data.token` to join get 'Invite not found'. Return `newToken.token` (or the generated `token`).
findings.failureMode: For an admin POST /v2/teams/:teamId/invite, body.data.token is a static team identifier rather than the issued verification token.
findings.title: Return the generated token, not its identifier

findings.description: The changed condition sends org/subteam links to `/teams?token=...` instead of `/signup?token=...&callbackUrl=...`. For a new user invited to an org, the `/teams` page redirects unauthenticated visitors to `/auth/login` and never shows the signup form, so recipients cannot accept the shareable link. For regular teams it now sends `/signup`, whose token pre-populates the form with the non-email identifier `invite-link-for-teamId-<id>`; restore the original branch so regular teams use `/teams` and org context uses `/signup`.
findings.failureMode: Unauthenticated org invitee follows issued inviteLink and lands on login rather than signup, while regular team invitee lands on signup with an invalid pre-filled email.
findings.title: Route organization invites to signup, not login

Use the existing `TeamService` export from `@calcom/platform-libraries` as the organization invite controller does.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint on new controller reports noRestrictedImports error and rejects the PR/commit.

findings.description: A normal workflow run stores inputs/outputs using `json.dumps` with the default `ensure_ascii=True` (e.g. `中文` is persisted as `\\u4e2d\\u6587`). Before this change the search keyword was converted to that representation, but the new raw `escape_like_pattern(keyword_trimmed)` leaves literal `中文`; searching workflow logs by this text now returns zero instead of the matching run. Apply JSON Unicode encoding for the inputs/outputs LIKE conditions before escaping their LIKE metacharacters (session ID search can use the raw escaped term).
findings.failureMode: Workflow app log keyword filtering misses non-ASCII text stored in JSON inputs/outputs
findings.title: Retain JSON-escaped keyword matching in workflow logs

findings.description: A successful ClickZetta connection is explicitly configured in quote-only string-literal mode. The Python `ESCAPE '\\\\'` here produces the SQL literal `ESCAPE '\\'` with **two** backslashes, rather than the one-character escape that SQL LIKE expects. When MATCH_ALL raises and `_search_by_like` runs, even searching for a plain term causes a SQL error rather than returning matching documents. Emit a single backslash in quote mode (or use a matching alternative escape and parameterize the pattern).
findings.failureMode: ClickZetta fallback full-text lookup raises SQL error after inverted-index lookup fails
findings.title: Give ClickZetta LIKE a one-character escape

findings.description: When `IRIS_TEXT_INDEX` is false, the fallback binds `escape_like_pattern(query)` (which prefixes `%` and `_` with `\\`) but the new SQL specifies `ESCAPE '|'`. A search for `50%` thus misses a document containing `50% discount`; a query ending in `|` can also escape the trailing `%` instead of matching normally. Set the SQL ESCAPE to a single backslash so it matches the helper's generated pattern.
findings.failureMode: IRIS fallback full-text search misses literal wildcard and pipe terms
findings.title: Use backslash as the IRIS LIKE escape character

findings.description: For a MySQL deployment with `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` enabled, a `not contains` metadata filter with a value such as `a_b` now generates `NOT LIKE '%a\\_b%'` without an `ESCAPE` clause. MySQL uses **no** default escape in this mode, so a record containing literal `a_b` is kept instead of excluded (and records with `a\\xb` can be misclassified). The other three branches pass `escape="\\"`; pass it here too.
findings.failureMode: Wrong document filtering for metadata not-contains with wildcard characters on MySQL NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES
findings.title: Supply ESCAPE to metadata not-contains

findings.description: `HSETEX key KEEPTTL FIELDS 1 field value` needs seven objects, but the changed rewrite passes `argc=6`, so the vector ends at `field` and silently drops `newobj`. Every HINCRBYFLOAT therefore emits an invalid command to replicas and AOF; an AOF restart logs `wrong number of arguments for 'hsetex' command` and loads the pre-increment value instead, losing the increment. Pass 7 to the rewrite.
findings.failureMode: Replica update fails; after AOF restart the HINCRBYFLOAT increment is lost (AOF loader logs a wrong-arity error and continues).
findings.title: Pass seven arguments when rewriting HINCRBYFLOAT to HSETEX

findings.description: For a live expiring hash field, `HINCRBYFLOAT h f 1` passes only `HASH_SET_TAKE_VALUE`. `hashTypeSet` clears the TTL for both LISTPACK_EX and HT encodings, so the primary returns HTTL=-1 instead of the original deadline and the existing HINCRBYFLOAT TTL test fails. The rewrite for replication does not update the primary; restore `HASH_SET_KEEP_TTL` on this local write.
findings.failureMode: Live field expiration silently lost on the primary on every HINCRBYFLOAT, contrary to existing behavior and test.
findings.title: Preserve field TTL on the primary before replication

findings.description: `addHashFieldToReply` is used only inside t_hash.c but this change removes `static`. It now appears as a global text symbol in t_hash.o (`nm -g`), violating the repository rule that file-local helpers have internal linkage and allowing a duplicate-name helper in a linked component to cause a linker collision. Restore `static`.
findings.failureMode: File-local helper becomes an externally visible symbol (confirmed by nm) and can cause link-time duplicate symbols.
findings.title: Keep the internal reply helper static

findings.description: The new adapter returns `None` when an injected `code_executor` returns `{}` or `{"result": None}`; its `isinstance` guard explicitly skips None. `TemplateTransformNode._run` then calls `len(None)` and crashes instead of producing a failed node result. The focused basedpyright run also reports `str | None` cannot satisfy its `str` return annotation. Reject `None` alongside other non-strings.
findings.failureMode: Injected code executor returning absent/null result leads to unhandled TypeError during template node execution; type-check fails.
findings.title: Reject null template results before returning

findings.description: When `template_renderer` implements `__len__` and is empty (or otherwise has false boolean value), this `or` replaces it with the sandbox adapter; the same fallback occurs for direct TemplateTransformNode injection at template_transform_node.py:41. A caller supplying e.g. an empty caching renderer sees the wrong renderer used and an unexpected sandbox invocation. Test `is not None` in both places.
